title: FlyWire: the complete map of neurons in the Drosophila brain
summary: Connectome of the adult Drosophila brain: nearly 140,000 neurons, over 15 million synaptic connections, and over 8,000 cell types. The page says deep neural networks segmented images and extracted neurons, but automated segmentation had millions of errors and required about 33 years of human correction across over 50 labs and citizen scientists.
organization: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Princeton, and FlyWire

evidence.tested: The connectome was checked against an earlier partial map, and connectomes were found to be highly consistent between animals.
evidence.unknown: About 0.5% of neurons have developmental wiring defects, connection signs were predicted rather than measured, and the dataset was not built for a specific medical application.
evidence.ai_role: Deep neural networks segmented electron microscopy images and extracted neurons; the first automated pass had millions of errors and was corrected by humans.
